subject: [COMPANY] <> Encord introduction
text:
Hi [NAME],

Nice to meet you, [SENDER] kindly shared your details.

I saw the work you're doing at [COMPANY]. Since you're manually tagging
whale and dolphin sounds on spectrograms, we could significantly speed this
up.

We've built an MLOps platform for granular audio annotation with
synchronised spectrogram and waveform segmentation - enabling faster, more
precise sound detection & labelling. You can also plug in your existing
edge models to pre-label sounds, so your team only verifies and refines
instead of starting from scratch.

If you're generating embeddings, our tool also lets you visualise clusters,
surface similar vocalisations, and identify rare outliers.

Would love to connect and share how we're supporting frontier audio labs
like Gradium (Kyutai) and Udio - sharing my diary link
<[LINK]>
 here.

text:

Working with teams at Reducto, AppFolio, and UiPath, we've seen a

extraction accuracy to reliably surfacing failures - layout drift, OCR

subject: ML Pipelines
text:
Hi [NAME],

I've been following what [COMPANY] is doing with conversational
intelligence - building reliable ML on messy, real-world audio is one of
the harder problems in voice AI right now.

One pattern we keep seeing: as model iterations speed up, the bottleneck
shifts to evaluating whether the new version actually sounds better across
edge cases like overlapping speakers or low-confidence transcriptions.
Comparing outputs side by side at scale is a real pain.

That's the core problem we solve at Encord. Leading AI teams such as
Synthesia and Twelve Labs use us to cut audio review cycles and catch
regressions before they ship.

Worth an intro call to see if this maps to what you're running into?
